subject: The weirdest trade I saw this month
preview_text: A user uploaded a photo of their cat. The verdict? 78% confidence. You won't believe what happened next.
body_paragraphs: Last week, someone uploaded a screenshot of their cat's food bowl. No chart. No numbers. Just a photo of kibble. The app gave them a trading verdict with 78% confidence. I thought it was a bug — until I checked the logs.

Turns out, they were using the app not for crypto, but for random decisions. Should I buy this stock? Eat that? Go to bed? The AI didn't care. It analyzed the 'chart' of the bowl's pattern and spat out a signal anyway. And they followed it. Made money on a meme coin an hour later.

That's when I realized: you can upload anything. A napkin sketch. A screenshot of your friend's watchlist. Even the Fear & Greed index you clipped from Twitter. The AI doesn't judge — it just reads structure and gives you a readout. It's like having a sober friend at 3am who tells you what the data actually says.

Open the app, upload something random. A receipt. A tweet. A photo of your dog. See what the AI says. I bet it surprises you. P.S. — One user uploaded a photo of their ceiling crack and got a 'strong sell' signal on their altcoin position. They sold. Coin dumped 12% an hour later. Not saying it's magic, but...
